result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers center the content, pad the header's .inner and main, keep the green header band full-width, and leave pre scrollable. A's 70ch cap fits the comfortable line length the rubric asks for. B's 800px cap gives about 760px of text, roughly 90+ characters per line at 17px Georgia, which is too long. Both repeat the whole stylesheet instead of showing only the changed rules, and B also says only two rules changed while adding a split rule. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B caps the text at 70ch, which gives a comfortable line length that scales with the font. A's 800px cap gives a 760px text area, roughly 85-90 characters of 17px Georgia, which is a bit wide. Both pad the header and main text, keep the full-width green header band, and leave pre scrollable. Neither shows only the changed rules, but B edits the existing rules in place, while A restructures them and its note that only two rules changed is inaccurate.
